questions.stem:
The Supreme Court recently intervened in the conduct of Urban Local Body elections in Andhra Pradesh, directing the State Election Commission (SEC) to postpone the publication of the final candidate list. With reference to the constitutional position of State Election Commissions in India, consider the following statements:
1. The State Election Commission is constituted under Article 243K of the Constitution for elections to Panchayats and under Article 243ZA for Municipalities.
2. The State Election Commissioner can be removed from office only through impeachment by Parliament, similar to the procedure prescribed for the removal of the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 243K constitutes the SEC for panchayat elections and Article 243ZA extends this to municipalities, making it a constitutional authority analogous to the ECI. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 243K(2) provides that the State Election Commissioner is removable only in like manner and on like grounds as a High Court judge, not through presidential-style impeachment by Parliament.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Andhra Pradesh SEC halts election process for 100 ULBs after Supreme Court order
questions.pyqLink: Tests Articles 243K/243ZA on State Election Commissions, a recurring static theme (cf. UPSC questions on ECI vs SEC powers).

questions.stem:
The Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy referred to the next phase of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) while discussing agrivoltaics. Consider the following statements about PM-KUSUM:
1. It is implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
2. It has three components, including the solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps.
3. Farmers can sell surplus solar power generated under the scheme to the grid for additional income.
4. The scheme mandates compulsory conversion of farmland into solar parks, discontinuing agricultural use.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: It is implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
It has three components, including the solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps.
Farmers can sell surplus solar power generated under the scheme to the grid for additional income.
The scheme mandates compulsory conversion of farmland into solar parks, discontinuing agricultural use.
questions.explanation: Statements 1-3 are correct: PM-KUSUM is an MNRE scheme with components for decentralised solar plants, standalone solar pumps and feeder-level solarisation, and it allows surplus power sale to the grid. Statement 4 is incorrect and contradicts the very premise of agrivoltaics, which the article describes as retaining agricultural production alongside power generation, not discontinuing it.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Agrivoltaics on 10% of suitable land can meet 2050 power demand: Pralhad Joshi
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional detail of a flagship renewable energy scheme, in the style of PYQs on scheme components and nodal ministries.

questions.stem:
ICAR-CMFRI launched an open-sea mussel longline farming unit at Vizhinjam under a Blue Growth Project. Consider the following pairs:
Term : Description
1. Agrivoltaics : Combines agricultural cultivation with solar photovoltaic power generation on the same land
2. Blue Growth Initiative : A programme promoting sustainable development of fisheries and aquaculture resources
3. CMFRI : An ICAR institute mandated with marine fisheries research
4. Mussel farming : Requires regular supplementary feed inputs since mussels are carnivorous filter feeders
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Agrivoltaics
Combines agricultural cultivation with solar photovoltaic power generation on the same land
Blue Growth Initiative
A programme promoting sustainable development of fisheries and aquaculture resources
CMFRI
An ICAR institute mandated with marine fisheries research
Mussel farming
Requires regular supplementary feed inputs since mussels are carnivorous filter feeders
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is incorrect: mussels are filter feeders that derive nutrition from naturally occurring phytoplankton and organic matter in seawater, which is precisely why open-sea mussel farming is low-input and does not require supplementary feed, unlike carnivorous finfish aquaculture.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: CMFRI launches open-sea mussel longline farming unit at Vizhinjam
questions.pyqLink: Tests static concepts of mariculture/bivalve ecology fused with the CMFRI news item, similar to PYQ pairs on species-habitat matching.

questions.stem: With reference to the term 'Agrivoltaics', which one of the following best describes it?
options: A technique of growing crops exclusively inside greenhouses powered by rooftop solar panels
A land-use approach that enables simultaneous agricultural production and solar photovoltaic electricity generation on the same parcel of land
A method of using crop residue and agricultural waste as biomass feedstock for solar-thermal power plants
A certification mechanism for rating farms on their carbon-neutral energy consumption
questions.explanation: Agrivoltaics refers to co-locating solar photovoltaic installations with ongoing agricultural activity on the same land, as described in the TERI study cited in the article, allowing farmers to retain crop income while also earning from power generation. The other options describe unrelated concepts: greenhouse solar farming, biomass-to-solar-thermal conversion, and a hypothetical certification scheme.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Agrivoltaics on 10% of suitable land can meet 2050 power demand: Pralhad Joshi
questions.pyqLink: Tests precise conceptual definition, in the style of PYQs like 'Which one of the following best describes the term Merchant Discount Rate?'

questions.stem:
With reference to the India-Australia defence relationship, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: AUSTRAHIND is a bilateral army exercise between India and Australia focused on joint operations in island and coastal environments under UN mandate provisions.
Statement-II: India and Australia are members, along with the United States and Japan, of the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), which has expanded defence cooperation between the two countries.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct: AUSTRAHIND is indeed a bilateral India-Australia army exercise themed on joint sub-conventional operations in island and coastal terrain, and both countries are Quad members. However, Statement-II does not explain Statement-I, since AUSTRAHIND originates from a dedicated bilateral defence cooperation framework and Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between India and Australia, not from their joint Quad membership.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India-Australia joint military exercise begins in capital
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between bilateral defence exercises and multilateral groupings, a format used since 2022 PYQs on explanatory-reasoning pairs.

questions.stem:
The open-sea mussel farming unit launched at Vizhinjam, Kerala, draws attention to India's maritime zones and the legal regime governing offshore resource use. Consider the following statements:
1. India's Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline, within which India has sovereign rights over living and non-living resources.
2. Open-sea mariculture activities such as mussel and cage-fish farming in India are undertaken within the territorial waters and the Exclusive Economic Zone.
3. The continental shelf of India, as recognised under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, extends uniformly up to 350 nautical miles from the coast in every part of the country.
4. Vizhinjam, where the mussel farming project was launched, lies on the west coast of India in Kerala.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: India's Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline, within which India has sovereign rights over living and non-living resources.
Open-sea mariculture activities such as mussel and cage-fish farming in India are undertaken within the territorial waters and the Exclusive Economic Zone.
The continental shelf of India, as recognised under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, extends uniformly up to 350 nautical miles from the coast in every part of the country.
Vizhinjam, where the mussel farming project was launched, lies on the west coast of India in Kerala.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: the EEZ extends to 200 nautical miles, India's open-sea mariculture projects (including the Vizhinjam unit) operate within territorial waters/EEZ, and Vizhinjam is on Kerala's west coast. Statement 3 is incorrect because the continental shelf is not uniformly 350 nautical miles everywhere; under UNCLOS it is normally 200 nautical miles, extendable up to 350 nautical miles only where geological criteria are met and a claim is approved by the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: CMFRI launches open-sea mussel longline farming unit at Vizhinjam
questions.pyqLink: Tests UNCLOS maritime zone definitions (territorial waters, EEZ, continental shelf), a recurring static geography/polity-fusion theme.

questions.stem:
In the Kovalam spa case, Kerala Police invoked provisions of the anti-human trafficking law. Consider the following statements regarding the legal framework against human trafficking in India:
1. The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 is the principal law in India dealing with trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation.
2. Section 370 of the Indian Penal Code, which specifically penalises trafficking of persons, was inserted through the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.
3. Offences under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act can be investigated only by the National Investigation Agency, and State police have no jurisdiction over such cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 is the principal law in India dealing with trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation.
Section 370 of the Indian Penal Code, which specifically penalises trafficking of persons, was inserted through the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.
Offences under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act can be investigated only by the National Investigation Agency, and State police have no jurisdiction over such cases.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the ITPA, 1956 remains the principal anti-trafficking law, and Section 370 IPC on trafficking of persons was inserted by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013. Statement 3 is incorrect, as ITPA offences are ordinarily investigated by State/local police (as in the Kovalam case, investigated by a State-level Special Investigation Team); the NIA's jurisdiction is limited to scheduled offences under the NIA Act, not an exclusive mandate over all trafficking cases.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Kerala Police to conduct intelligence-based operations against spas: Ravada Chandrasekhar
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory detail on anti-trafficking law and investigating authority, similar to PYQs distinguishing statutory bodies' jurisdiction.

questions.stem: The dissolution of the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (Kargil) and the announcement of fresh panchayat elections in Ladakh draw attention to the legal framework of local self-government in Union Territories. Consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils were constituted under the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution.
Ladakh is a Union Territory without a legislature, administered through a Lieutenant Governor.
Panchayats in India derive their constitutional status from the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which inserted Part IX into the Constitution.
The term of a Panchayat or an Autonomous Hill Council is five years, and this term can be extended indefinitely by the appropriate legislature during a national emergency.
questions.explanation: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct. LAHDCs are statutory bodies under the LAHDC Act, 1997, not Sixth Schedule bodies — Ladakh is not a Sixth Schedule area. Article 243E caps extension of a dissolved Panchayat's term at six months after an emergency ceases, not indefinitely.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Ladakh administration dissolves hill council in Kargil, announces panchayat elections on November 21
questions.pyqLink: Tests Sixth Schedule vs statutory hill councils and Article 243E; similar to UPSC 2015 question on Panchayati Raj provisions.

questions.stem: The seizure of a licensed sporting rifle from persons suspected of deer hunting in a Karnataka forest draws attention to India's wildlife protection law. Consider the following statements: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended in 2022, currently provides for four schedules, with Schedule I species granting the highest degree of protection.
A valid arms licence under the Arms Act, 1959 permits its holder to hunt Schedule I species without any further permission.
Deer species such as chital and sambar are accorded legal protection under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Hunting offences involving Schedule I species under the Act are treated as cognizable offences.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. The 2022 amendment reduced the schedules from six to four; deer species remain protected; and Schedule I offences are cognizable with enhanced penalties. Statement 2 is false — an arms licence only governs lawful possession of a firearm and never authorises hunting of a protected species.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Three held for suspected deer hunt in Karnataka; rifle, night-vision equipment seized in Hyderabad
questions.pyqLink: Tests Wildlife (Protection) Act schedules and offences; similar in spirit to UPSC questions on Schedule I/II species protection.

questions.stem: With reference to the weather system currently bringing heavy rainfall to Tamil Nadu, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The northeast monsoon, which supplies the bulk of Tamil Nadu's annual rainfall, occurs when winds retreating from the Indian subcontinent pick up moisture crossing the Bay of Bengal.
Low-pressure systems associated with the northeast monsoon typically originate over the Arabian Sea and move eastward into Tamil Nadu.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the northeast (retreating) monsoon of October-December is Tamil Nadu's principal rainfall source, with winds gathering moisture over the Bay of Bengal. Statement 2 is wrong: as the article confirms, the low-pressure system formed over the southwest Bay of Bengal, not the Arabian Sea.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Fresh weather system to fuel another spell of heavy rain in Tamil Nadu
questions.pyqLink: Tests the mechanism of the northeast monsoon; recurring UPSC theme on Indian monsoon systems and retreating monsoon.

questions.stem: The Central Water Commission's flood warning names several Tamil Nadu rivers. Consider the following statements about these rivers. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Tamirabharani originates in the Western Ghats and flows entirely within Tamil Nadu before draining into the Gulf of Mannar.
The Vaigai is a tributary of the Cauvery and joins it near Tiruchirappalli.
The Bhavani, a tributary of the Cauvery, originates in the Nilgiri hills of the Western Ghats.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Tamirabharani rises in the Pothigai hills and is the rare Tamil Nadu river flowing wholly within the state into the Gulf of Mannar; the Bhavani rises in the Nilgiris and joins the Cauvery. Statement 2 is false — the Vaigai is an independent river rising in the Western Ghats near Theni and draining towards the Palk Strait, not a Cauvery tributary.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Fresh weather system to fuel another spell of heavy rain in Tamil Nadu
questions.pyqLink: Tests peninsular river geography; similar to UPSC questions on origin and course of south Indian rivers.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs regarding the restored Poosi Forest Palace and its colonial-era context. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Poosi Forest Palace
Built in 1850 by Srinivasa Rao Sahib, the Jagir of Arani, as a hunting camp
Spencer Plaza, Chennai
Designed by the same architect who built the Poosi Forest Palace, William Pogson
Madras Presidency
One of the original Presidencies of British India, alongside Bombay and Bengal
Jagir system
A land tenure under which the Crown directly collected land revenue with no intermediary
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched per the article and static facts about the Madras Presidency. Pair 4 is wrong — the jagir system was precisely the opposite of direct Crown collection; it assigned revenue rights to an intermediary, the jagirdar, which is why Srinivasa Rao Sahib held the title 'Jagir of Arani'.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Forest Department restores Poosi Forest Palace near Arani for public viewing
questions.pyqLink: Tests colonial administrative/land-revenue systems (jagirdari vs ryotwari); recurring UPSC theme on British land revenue systems.

questions.stem: With reference to the legal basis of bodies such as the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council, whose dissolution in Kargil was announced this week, which one of the following best describes such Hill Councils?
options: They are constitutional bodies created under the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution, applicable to the tribal areas of Ladakh.
They are statutory bodies established under a specific Act for the region, exercising delegated administrative, financial and developmental functions, without enjoying constitutional status.
They are constitutional bodies functioning under Part IX of the Constitution on the same footing as Gram Panchayats.
They are purely executive bodies created by an administrative order of the Ministry of Home Affairs, without any legislative backing.
questions.explanation: LAHDCs were created under the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils Act, 1997 — a statutory, not constitutional, arrangement, which is why they can be dissolved and reconstituted by executive notification following district reorganisation. Ladakh is not a Sixth Schedule area (option A), LAHDCs are distinct from Part IX panchayats (option C), and they do rest on a legislative Act, not a bare administrative order (option D).
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Ladakh administration dissolves hill council in Kargil, announces panchayat elections on November 21
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory vs constitutional local bodies; relevant to Sixth Schedule vs Part IX/statutory council distinctions asked in past UPSC papers.

questions.stem: With reference to the seizure of a licensed sporting rifle from persons suspected of deer hunting in Karnataka, consider the following two statements.
statements: Statement-I: Possession of a licensed sporting rifle does not exempt a person from prosecution for hunting a protected wild animal.

Statement-II: A valid arms licence under the Arms Act, 1959 only regulates the lawful possession and use of a firearm, and does not by itself authorise the hunting of any wild animal protected under wildlife law.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I: an Arms Act licence governs only lawful possession of the weapon, so using even a licensed firearm to hunt a protected species remains an offence under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, independent of the firearm's legality.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Three held for suspected deer hunt in Karnataka; rifle, night-vision equipment seized in Hyderabad
questions.pyqLink: Tests the interaction between the Arms Act, 1959 and Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972; static-law application format introduced from UPSC 2022 onward.

questions.stem: With reference to the diversion of forest land in India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires prior approval of the Central Government before forest land is diverted for any non-forest purpose.
The Forest Advisory Committee is a constitutional body vested with final authority to approve or reject proposals for diversion of forest land.
Compensatory afforestation is normally required to be carried out on non-forest land equivalent in extent to the forest land diverted.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 bars state governments from diverting forest land for non-forest use without prior Central approval. Statement 3 is correct, as reflected in the NHPC Kamala project case, where compensatory afforestation is proposed on non-forest land in Madhya Pradesh since Arunachal Pradesh lacks suitable local land. Statement 2 is wrong: the Forest Advisory Committee is a statutory/administrative body constituted under the Act to examine and recommend proposals, not a constitutional body with final approval power, which rests with the Central Government.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: NHPC seeks Forest clearance to fell over 23 lakh trees for Kamala hydel project in Arunachal
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 and compensatory afforestation mechanism, similar to UPSC 2022 questions on forest diversion and the Compensatory Afforestation Fund.

questions.stem: With reference to India's trade relations, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under the Most Favoured Nation (MFN) principle of the WTO, a member country must extend equally favourable trade terms to all other members, subject to recognised exceptions such as free trade agreements and customs unions.
India extends Most Favoured Nation status to a trading partner only after concluding a bilateral Free Trade Agreement with that country.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly describes the MFN principle under GATT/WTO, non-discrimination among members with FTAs/customs unions as recognised exceptions. Statement 2 is incorrect: MFN status is a general WTO obligation that applies automatically among member countries by virtue of membership, not something granted only after signing a separate FTA; India and the US, for instance, currently negotiating a bilateral trade deal, already extend MFN treatment to each other as WTO members.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: 'Pretty close': Trump hints at 'much different kind of deal' with India
questions.pyqLink: Tests the WTO's Most Favoured Nation principle, similar to UPSC 2022 question on WTO agreements and India's trade commitments.

questions.stem: With reference to minority educational institutions in India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Article 30 of the Constitution guarantees only religious minorities, and not linguistic minorities, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
A State Legislature can, by an ordinary Act, create a new statutory authority to regulate educational institutions within the State and replace an earlier statutory body performing that function.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: education falls in the Concurrent List, and a State Legislature can enact an ordinary law to dissolve an existing statutory body and create a new one, as Uttarakhand did by abolishing the Madrasa Education Board and creating USAME under the Uttarakhand Minority Education Act, 2025. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 30 explicitly protects both religious and linguistic minorities, not religious minorities alone.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Uttarakhand ends Friday off for madrasas as CM Dhami bats for uniform system
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 30 minority rights and the nature of statutory bodies created by legislative Acts, a recurring polity theme in UPSC prelims.

questions.stem: Food safety authorities in India have periodically seized snacks and sweets found to contain unauthorised colouring agents such as Rhodamine B and Metanil Yellow. Which one of the following best describes the significance of banning such substances?
options: They are preservatives added to extend the shelf life of packaged snacks, and were banned solely due to concerns over import duty evasion.
They are naturally occurring plant-based pigments banned only because they alter the nutritional value of processed food without posing any health risk.
They are genetically modified organisms used in confectionery production, prohibited under India's biosafety regulations.

They are synthetic colours sometimes illegally added to foods like sweets and snacks to enhance appearance, and are banned because they are non-permitted additives with carcinogenic potential under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
questions.explanation: Rhodamine B and Metanil Yellow are synthetic dyes not approved for food use under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, and are banned because of their carcinogenic and toxicological risk, not because of duty evasion, nutrition loss, or GMO status. The Maharashtra FDA's seizure of coloured wafers and sweets suspected of containing such unauthorised colouring reflects this regulatory concern.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Banned tobacco, suspect snacks seized in Mumbai; FDA crackdown nets ₹3.11 crore across Maharashtra
questions.pyqLink: Tests awareness of food adulteration and permitted/banned food additives under the FSSA, 2006, similar to UPSC questions on food safety standards and health hazards of synthetic additives.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of rivers of the Eastern Himalayan/Brahmaputra system and their description. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Kamala River
Right-bank tributary of the Subansiri River
Subansiri River
Originates in Tibet and is a major tributary of the Brahmaputra River
Siang River
Known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet before entering India and becoming the Brahmaputra
Kameng River
A left-bank tributary of the Teesta River
questions.explanation: Kamala, Subansiri and Siang are correctly matched: Kamala is a right-bank tributary of the Subansiri, which itself joins the Brahmaputra after originating in Tibet, while the Siang is the Indian stretch of the Yarlung Tsangpo before it becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam. The Kameng-Teesta pair is wrong: the Kameng is a tributary of the Brahmaputra in its own right, while the Teesta is an entirely separate river system flowing through Sikkim and West Bengal.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: NHPC seeks Forest clearance to fell over 23 lakh trees for Kamala hydel project in Arunachal
questions.pyqLink: Tests river systems and tributaries of the Brahmaputra in Arunachal Pradesh, a recurring geography theme similar to UPSC questions on Himalayan river origins and confluences.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's institutional and legal framework against narcotics. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 is the primary legislation governing offences related to drug trafficking and consumption in India.
The Narcotics Control Bureau functions under the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.
The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan (Drug-Free India Campaign) is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Possession of any quantity of a narcotic drug for personal consumption is treated as a non-bailable offence under the NDPS Act.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the NDPS Act, 1985 is the core law on narcotics offences, the Narcotics Control Bureau operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs, and the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Statement 4 is incorrect because the NDPS Act grades punishment by quantity (small, intermediate, commercial); offences involving a small quantity for personal consumption attract lighter, generally bailable, punishment rather than being automatically non-bailable.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Ensure India is drug free by December 2029: Amit Shah to police forces
questions.pyqLink: Tests the NDPS Act's quantity-based punishment structure and nodal ministries for anti-drug schemes, similar to past UPSC questions on NCB and NDPS Act provisions.
